qc.label_under_test: The 'as', or the 'a' right after me, us or you, when a label bounces back at me, us or you: an earlier clause has me, us or you seeing, calling, regarding, treating or describing someone else as something, and a following clause has that other person or group label me, us or you in return, either with 'as' (they saw me as a fool) or bare with 'a' (he called me a liar). Weaker: the same two-way swap between named people or third-person pronouns. Weak: a one-way label of me, us or you with no earlier clause; me labelled first and then answering back; a plural bare return with no 'as' or 'a' (named us cowards); a return aimed at a third party; official appointments to a post.

neighbours.label: On the word right after me or us (often 'as', 'a', 'for', 'of', 'my' or 'our') when a judgement bounces back: an earlier clause has me or us judging another person or group (labelling them, seeing them as something, praising, blaming, thanking, admiring, criticising, rewarding, punishing or forgiving them), and a following clause has that person or group return the same kind of judgement to me or us. Weaker: the same two-way swap between third-person pronouns. Silent: a one-way judgement of me or us with no earlier clause; me or us judged first and then answering back; an ordinary returned action that is not a judgement (visiting, phoning, paying, lending, hugging back); a judgement aimed at a thing rather than a person.
fire: We saw them as rivals, and they saw us as rivals too.
I praised her for her patience, and she praised me for mine.
We thanked the volunteers, and they thanked us for our support.
I called him a genius, and he called me a genius right back.
We blamed the other team, and they blamed us for the delay.
I admired the old sailor, and he admired me for my courage.
We forgave our neighbours, and in turn they forgave us for our noise.
I criticised the coach, and the coach criticised me for my attitude.
quiet: They saw us as rivals from the very first match.
She praised me for my patience during the long meeting.
They blamed us first, and we blamed them for the delay.
We visited our cousins, and they visited us for the holidays.
I phoned my sister, and she phoned me back an hour later.
We lent them a ladder, and they lent us a drill for the weekend.
I hugged my grandfather, and he hugged me back tightly.
We admired the cathedral, and the guide showed us around the nave.

predictions: blind test (label-only second author); expect most fire items above 0.20 and the 'visited us for' near miss as the main risk
